summary: All three Self Employed runs read as plausible accounts for the businesses described: the two BrickWork Pro runs show construction-appropriate materials, sub-contractor and motor costs with a labourer's payroll of 18,000 and Employment-Allowance-nil employer NI, VAT boxes nil for the unregistered trader and 7,809 due for the registered one on the same underlying profit; the Precision Code consultancy shows payroll as its largest cost, real depreciation and disposals, and income tax and Class 4 NI at credible rates on a 144,715 profit. The concerns recorded are all figures that reconcile once the product's stated treatments are applied, and none of them blocks the run.

concerns.figure: Capital allowances 12,000 / fixed asset additions 12,000 (Fixedassets Schedule Q1, FAreconciliation E11, SA103S D80) in se-brickwork-pro-vat
concerns.where: se-brickwork-pro-vat: Fixed asset checks and SA103S Capital allowances
concerns.why: The VAT scenario's fa-coded purchases total 14,400.00 including VAT, so the net cost that should reach the asset schedule is 12,000.00 — which is exactly what is reported. This is the same 12,000 as the non-VAT run whose journal was 12,000 net, so both reconcile as designed and this is not a discrepancy. Noted only because the identical figure across a VAT and a non-VAT run invites a second look.

concerns.figure: Sub-Contractors 6,666.67 against Wages & Salaries 92,735.73 (P&L B15 / B21) in se-scenario-advanced
concerns.why: For an IT consultancy the cost mix is credible (payroll dominates, small stock and direct costs), but the c-coded 8,000 gross journal lands in a caption labelled Sub-Contractors while stock-coded purchases of 6,540 gross produce a Materials line of 9,450 after the 4,000 stock fall. Worth a reader confirming that a software consultancy is meant to carry 10,000 opening and 6,000 closing stock at all.

concerns.figure: SA103S Taxable profit 142,632.06 vs Net profit for tax calc 144,715.39 (SE Short D99 / D106) in se-scenario-advanced
concerns.why: The two lines differ by 2,083.33, which is exactly the Grants Received figure on the P&L (B11). The scenario notes state D106 = D99 + grants and that tax is charged on the higher figure, so this reconciles and is not a fault; recorded only so a reader can tie the two lines together.
